Package de.labathome.trustconstr.records

Class PreparedConstraint

java.lang.Object
de.labathome.trustconstr.records.PreparedConstraint
public class PreparedConstraint extends Object
User-facing constraint prepared for use by the trust-constr orchestrator. Mirrors scipy's PreparedConstraint (scipy/optimize/_constraints.py:352): wraps the constraint in an appropriate VectorFunctionLike carrier (with f and J cached at x0), exposes the bounds and per-row keep-feasible mask, and validates that x0 satisfies any keep-feasible inequality rows.

Three constructors handle the three constraint shapes scipy supports: LinearConstraint (uses LinearVectorFunction), NonlinearConstraint (uses NonlinearVectorFunction), Bounds (uses IdentityVectorFunction).

  • Constructor Details

    • PreparedConstraint

      public PreparedConstraint(LinearConstraint lc, Matrix x0, Optional<Boolean> sparseJacobian)
      Prepare a LinearConstraint. f and J are cached at x0 via a LinearVectorFunction.
      Parameters:
      lc - linear constraint
      x0 - starting iterate (n x 1)
      sparseJacobian - user preference for Jacobian representation; Optional.empty() preserves whatever lc.getA() already is

    • PreparedConstraint

      public PreparedConstraint(NonlinearConstraint nc, Matrix x0, Optional<Boolean> sparseJacobian, FiniteDifferenceBounds finiteDiffBounds)
      Prepare a NonlinearConstraint. f and J are cached at x0 via a NonlinearVectorFunction.
      Parameters:
      nc - nonlinear constraint
      x0 - starting iterate (n x 1)
      sparseJacobian - user preference for Jacobian representation
      finiteDiffBounds - bounds to clamp finite-difference perturbations within (currently unused -- the FD wrapping is done by NonlinearConstraint itself when the user omits an analytic Jacobian, before this constructor is reached)

    • PreparedConstraint

      public PreparedConstraint(Bounds bounds, Matrix x0, Optional<Boolean> sparseJacobian)
      Prepare Bounds (folding them into the constraint set as the trivial linear constraint lb &le; x &le; ub with A = I). f = x0 and J = I are cached via an IdentityVectorFunction.
      Parameters:
      bounds - box bounds on the decision variables
      x0 - starting iterate (n x 1)
      sparseJacobian - user preference for Jacobian representation

  • Method Details

    • violation

      public double[] violation(Matrix x)
      Compute the per-row constraint violation at x. Each row's violation is max(0, lb - f(x)) + max(0, f(x) - ub): the amount by which the constraint is exceeded on either side. Mirrors scipy's PreparedConstraint.violation.
      Parameters:
      x - current iterate (n x 1)
      Returns:
      per-row violation, length m()
